title: MetaRDK
description: MetaRDK contains intracranial EEG (stereo-EEG) high-gamma activity from patients with pharmacologically intractable epilepsy performing a perceptual random-dot motion decision task followed by a confidence judgement. The data comprise average power modulation in five non-overlapping frequency bands between 70 and 150 Hz, segmented from trial onset to trial offset and sampled at 512 Hz. Behavioral tables (stimulus onset, response times, confidence, changes of mind) accompany the recordings to study the neural correlates of decision making and metacognition.
methods_description: Patients with intractable epilepsy were recorded at the bedside with a Micromed system, with electrode implantation determined solely by clinical need. They performed a random-dot motion left/right discrimination task (6 s response window, difficulty titrated to 70% correct with an adaptive staircase), responding by mouse movement and click, then rated confidence on a 0-100 scale. Trials and channels with epilepsy-related artifacts were removed.
